Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vishnu Kumar Patil
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
Learned counsel for the informant is not present.

2. Heard Sri Yogesh Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Sunil Kumar,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicants seek bail in Case Crime No. 186 of 2024, U/S 498A, 323, 304B, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P.
Act, Police Station- Khairgarh, District- Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.
PROSECUTION STORY:

1

4. The applicant and other family members are stated to have forcibly administered certain poisonous material to the informant on 26.6.2024 at about 8.00 pm, whereby her condition deteriorated and she was admitted to hospital.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF THE APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence.
6. The FIR is delayed by about three months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

7. There is an application moved by the informant herself, which has been filed as Annexure-4 to the affidavit accompanying the bail application, which categorically states that out of rage, she herself had consumed the toilet cleaner, as such, it is a clear cut case of false implication.
8. Subsequent to the institution of the FIR, the informant had expired.
The cause of death in the said post-mortem report was due to "cardio respiratory failure as a result of septicemia", as such, the informant had expired due to infection sustained by her.
After being admitted to the hospital due to consumption of poisonous material, she was discharged and was hale and hearty.
9. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
10. The applicant is languishing in jail since 24.9.2024, having no criminal antecedent to his credit.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/STATE:
11. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application, but has not disputed the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicant.
CONCLUSION:
12. In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs.
Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785 this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

Ravidas vs State Of U.P. on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84149603/
2 13.

A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
14.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
15.
Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
16. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicants fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
17.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

18. Let the applicant- Ravidas involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
19. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicants and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

20. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
